SMTO-GML-0004 — SMTO can't find a Gmail account to use

GUID: 22779e27-2b30-495d-b735-6596fd098db9
Slug: gmail-account-missing
Domain: GML · Subsystem: gml

What happened

  • This request needs a Gmail account, but none is saved in SMTO, or the one mentioned doesn't exist or isn't allowed to do this kind of action.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open More options › Parameter Store and search for gmail. If your account is listed, check that your request mentions it with exactly that name. SMTO looks for the exact name, so a typo or renamed entry isn't found.
  2. If no account is listed, pick the Gmail — App Password (Gmail + SMTP) template, select New, enter your Gmail address and app password in the Value tab, and select Save. This saves a Gmail account SMTO can use for reading and sending mail.
  3. If your Gmail account signs in through Google instead, ask SMTO to connect it again. Finish the Google sign-in page that opens and allow the access it asks for. An account without permission for this kind of action isn't counted as usable.
  4. Write your request again and type @ to pick the Gmail account. Mentioning the account tells SMTO exactly which mailbox to use.

What success looks like

  • SMTO finds the account you mentioned and the Gmail request runs.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them to the person who manages SMTO. Never type your password or app password into a conversation; enter it only in Parameter Store.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • No usable Gmail account was found: the referenced parameter key does not exist or has another type, or automatic resolution found no eligible gmail_account, google_account or gmail_app_password_account for the required features.

What this means

  • Exact account/profile lookup finds no record, or automatic account resolution has no eligible accepted/stored account for the requested features. Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.

Why this can happen

  • Exact account/profile lookup finds no record, or automatic account resolution has no eligible accepted/stored account for the requested features.

How to diagnose it

  • Inspect explicit account_ref, accepted bindings and feature eligibility rather than choosing another account silently.

How to fix it

  • Check the exact parameter key in the request against Parameter Store. Create a gmail_app_password_account from the 'Gmail — App Password (Gmail + SMTP)' template or run the Gmail/Google connect flow so the account has the required feature scopes, then reference it explicitly; never put credentials in task text or command arguments.
  • Connect or select the intended Gmail account through the supported account flow.

Retry and execution caution

  • Apply the correction and confirm the relevant state before requesting another attempt. Prior completed work remains governed by its receipts.

How to verify the fix

  • The intended account is explicitly connected and selected in the supported scope.

What not to do

  • Do not put credentials in task text, command arguments, screenshots or diagnostic reports.

Technical notes

  • Gmail provider receipts and exact account/message identities determine effects. Authorization, pagination or presentation failure cannot undo a send or other mutation; diagnostic rendering performs no mailbox or OAuth request.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
